questions.prompt: The Dependency Rule constrains which kind of dependency?

options.text: The runtime flow of control — who calls whom

questions.explanation: The rule governs source-code dependencies (imports). It says nothing about the runtime flow of control, which often points the other way.

questions.prompt: How can a use case cause a presenter to run without violating the Dependency Rule?

options.text: By importing the presenter class directly
By calling through an output port — an interface the use case owns that the presenter implements
It cannot; use cases may never trigger presenters
By putting the presenter in the entities layer

questions.explanation: An output port lets control flow outward to the presenter while the source-code dependency (presenter → interface) still points inward.

questions.prompt: Data that crosses a boundary should be a simple data structure, often called a ______ — never an entity or an ORM row.
questions.explanation: A DTO (Data Transfer Object) / request-response model crosses boundaries so neither side depends on the other's internals.

questions.prompt: Which imports are ILLEGAL under the Dependency Rule (inner mentioning outer)? Select all that apply.

options.text: An entity imports the Postgres driver
A use case imports an HTTP controller
A use case imports an entity
An entity imports a use case

questions.explanation: Inner code may not mention outer code: an entity importing a driver, a use case importing a controller, and an entity importing a use case are all illegal. A use case importing an entity points inward and is fine.

questions.prompt: Order these from highest-level (furthest from I/O) to lowest-level (closest to I/O).
questions.explanation: 'Level' is distance from inputs and outputs; entities are highest-level (furthest from I/O), frameworks lowest. Lower levels depend on higher, never the reverse.

questions.prompt: Match each concept to its description.

pairs.right: Which code calls which at run time
An inner-owned interface control crosses outward through
A module's distance from inputs and outputs

questions.explanation: The rule constrains source-code dependencies; control flow can oppose them via ports; level orders the system by distance from I/O.
